question: How much will Crude Oil Futures total price returns exceed S&P 500 Futures in these biweekly periods of Q3 2026? (Sep 7 - Sep 18)

calls.reasoning: Reference class (2-week front-month WTI return minus S&P 500 futures return) has a long-run median near -0.5 pts, and the case-specific evidence is genuinely two-sided, so I stay near that anchor and put almost all the work into dispersion. Up: US-Iran strikes resumed this week, Hormuz transits fell to 6/day vs a ~13 average, the largest tanker operator sees no normalization by year-end, and the equity leg faces a Sep 16 FOMC with a hike ~66% priced into a market already at 4-week lows. Down: Oman-mediated Hormuz talks, OPEC+ having completed its 1.65 mb/d unwind with a Sep 6 JMMC, EIA/JPM Q3 Brent forecasts ~11% below spot, and the ordinary decay of a risk premium after a +9% week and +21% month. Neither side dominates and both are largely in the futures price already. What is not ordinary is the width: this market ran $115 in April to $68.58 on Jul 1 to $92 now, with a -7.5% and a +6.6% single session inside four days in July. Negative oil-equity correlation in this inflation-driven regime widens the spread further, and the Sep 16 FOMC reinforces it. I price 5% escape each way on named mechanisms (Kharg Island/full Hormuz closure up; signed deal unwinding the premium toward the ~$70 pre-war level down). No market prices this contract; the Polymarket/Kalshi WTI books have no equity leg and different deadlines, so they inform dispersion, not the level.
